simple.meaning: רָשַׁע (râshaʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to be (causatively, do or declare ) wrong ; by implication, to disturb , violate.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 36 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, and 8 more, beginning at Exodus 22:8. Its contexts include righteousness, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָשַׁע (H7561).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָשַׁע (râshaʻ) / H7561 is traced through Exodus 22:8, Deuteronomy 25:1, 1 Samuel 14:47, 1 Samuel 24:14 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: If the thief isn’t found, then the master of the house shall come near to God, to find out whether or not he has put his hand on his neighbor’s goods.
If there is a controversy between men, and they come to judgment and the judges judge them, then they shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked.

Now when Saul had taken the kingdom over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. Wherever he turned himself, he defeated them.
Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea?
For I have kept Yahweh’s ways,
then hear in heaven, and act, and judge your servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way on his own head, and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

yet if they repent in the land where they are carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication to you in the land of those who carried them captive, saying, ‘We have sinned, and have done perversely; we have dealt wickedly;’

yet if they come to their senses in the land where they are carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication to you in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have done perversely, and have dealt wickedly;’
After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel. The same did very wickedly.
He also walked in the ways of Ahab’s house, because his mother was his counselor in acting wickedly.
However you are just in all that has come on us; for you have dealt truly, but we have done wickedly.
Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me.
I will be condemned.
I will tell God, ‘Do not condemn me.
Although you know that I am not wicked,
If I am wicked, woe to me.
Your own mouth condemns you, and not I.
Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
Yes surely, God will not do wickedly,
Should even one who hates justice govern?
